title: Auth API 401/429 debugging scratchpad (Lena)
content:
Context:
- Intermittent 401s and 429s reported by a handful of customers since 2026-03-15. Pattern: usually after sustained burst of requests from a single API key; sometimes 401s then 429s for same key.
- Repro on staging: moderately reproducible when using a client that retries aggressively without backoff.

Repro steps (quick):
1) curl test using my dev key (KEY_DEV_XXX):
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY_DEV_XXX" \n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n     -d '{"input":"test"}' \n     https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate

   Observed: occasional 401 with body: "{\"error\":\"Unauthorized\"}" and headers: X-Request-Id: req_abc123

2) Burst test (100 reqs/s) using quick-loop (python locust style):
   - After ~60s, start seeing 429 responses: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
     Response body: {"error":"quota_exceeded","detail":"per-minute quota exceeded"}
     Headers observed (from edge): Retry-After: 10, x-rate-limit-limit: 600, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-request-id: req_456def

Commands & logs I collected:
- curl sample showing 401:
  > HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  > Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 15:22:10 GMT
  > Content-Type: application/json
  > x-request-id: req_abc123
  {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Invalid API key"}

- Edge logs (subset):
  2026-03-17T15:21:58Z [edge] req_abc120 key=KEY_DEV_XXX route=/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=34
  2026-03-17T15:22:02Z [edge] req_abc121 key=KEY_DEV_XXX route=/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=29
  2026-03-17T15:22:10Z [edge] req_abc123 key=KEY_DEV_XXX route=/v1/generate status=401 err=auth.failed msg="apikey not found in auth cache"
  2026-03-17T15:22:15Z [edge] req_abc124 key=KEY_DEV_XXX route=/v1/generate status=429 err=quota.exceeded window=60s limit=600 used=601

Hypotheses (brain dump):
- H1: Key rotation race (auth cache TTL + rotation job) -> key briefly invalidated server-side while downstream request still uses it.
  Evidence: auth.failed msg in edge logs referencing "auth cache". But customer keys are managed via KMS lookup + cache in auth service.
- H2: Aggressive retrying client causes simultaneous requests that exceed per-minute quota, producing 429s.
  Evidence: x-rate-limit-remaining drops to 0 then 429 with used=601 ~> limit=600.
- H3: There is a bug in the per-key rate limiter where 401s are returned if auth service times out under high load instead of returning a 429 or 503.
  Evidence: 401s appear right before 429s in timeline. Auth service traces show a 504 to edge at approx the same time.
- H4: Inconsistent enforcement between edge and origin: edge uses cached auth and quota counters, origin re-checks and occasionally returns 401 when it can't resolve key (race).

Experiments/troubleshooting performed:
- Replayed with a different key -> same pattern but at different absolute times (suggests not key-specific config).
- Disabled client-side retries -> reduced 429 symptom but still saw occasional 401s.
- Increased auth cache TTL on staging from 30s -> 5m -> reduced 401 frequency in short runs.
- Added exponential backoff in client -> smoother behavior, reduced 429s.
- Ran end-to-end trace: trace id req_abc123 shows auth service 503 for a small span (00:00:02) and edge returned 401 when upstream auth returned error.

Data to pull / next checks:
- [ ] Check K/V store (auth cache) eviction logs around 2026-03-17T15:21:50-15:23:00 for KEY_DEV_XXX and other affected keys.
- [ ] Query rate-limit DB: SELECT count(*) by minute for key=KEY_DEV_XXX between 15:20-15:25; check for bursts and spikes.
- [ ] Correlate auth service CPU/RPS during incident window - any GC pauses? OOM?
- [ ] Search for recent deploys to auth service / edge / rate-limiter around 2026-03-15..2026-03-17 (deploy tag?).
- [ ] Check HSM / KMS latencies - increased KMS latency could cause auth service timeouts, leading to 401 fallback.
- [ ] Pull full trace (X-Trace-Id) for req_abc123 and neighbors.

Proposed mitigations (short-term):
- Prevent auth service from returning 401 on internal auth-timeouts; prefer 503 or 429 depending on scenario. 401 should only be for explicit invalid credentials.
- Add jittered exponential backoff guidance in client SDK and add default retry/backoff in gateway rules when 429 seen.
- Increase auth cache TTL to 5m by default for staging and maybe prod for keys that rotate infrequently. Add signal for forced invalidation when rotation occurs.
- Implement guardrail in rate-limiter to return 429 with Retry-After headline instead of 401 when upstream auth lookup fails under load.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- TODO: open INFRA ticket with trace + logs (INFRA-332) and add sample curl + reproduction steps.
- TODO: schedule quick sync with Oliver + Jordan tomorrow 10:30am to align on deploys and mitigation.
- TODO: add a small script to ramp burst with controlled qps and capture headers for 1k test.

Questions for the team / unknowns:
- Is there any forced key rotation job that would flush auth cache for keys older than X days? Who owns that? (cc: @security)
- How do we want the semantic mapping between auth errors and HTTP codes to behave under transient failures? Current mapping seems leaky (401 used for timeouts).

Quick references / snippets:
- Rate-limit headers we expect on success responses: x-rate-limit-limit: <int>, x-rate-limit-remaining: <int>, Retry-After: <seconds> (when 429).
- Edge -> Auth behavior: edge caches key -> consults local rate-limiter -> forward to origin. If origin auth fails, edge currently surfaces 401. Need to change that.

Scratch ideas for long-term:
- Centralized per-key token bucket with distributed counters (Redis sharded) with coordinated decrement that can respond gracefully under partition.
- Prometheus alert if auth cache miss rate > 1% or auth lookup latency p95 > 200ms.
- Migration plan for keys with frequent rotation -> introduce ephemeral tokens with longer cache validity and rotation handshake.

Misc snippets (for convenience):
- Example curl for retry/backoff test:
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY_DEV_XXX" \n      https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate &
    sleep 0.01
  done

- Sample error body observed (429):
  {"error":"quota_exceeded","detail":"per-minute quota exceeded","code":429}

Footnotes:
- Keep this as a working doc; will convert to formal incident postmortem if we confirm root cause.
- If we escalate to product/support, include customer impact metrics: affected keys, percent errors, duration.

End of scratchpad.
